evaluation.results_summary: The developer reports that RecurrentGemma models perform on par with Gemma models while offering faster inference and lower memory use, especially for long sequences.
evaluation.safety_evals: The developer states that ethics and safety evaluation results met internal policy thresholds for categories including child safety, content safety, representational harms, memorization, and large-scale harms.

identity.name: recurrentgemma-2b-it
identity.summary: The 2B instruction-tuned version of the RecurrentGemma open language model family.

possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Gated access and license restrict external inspection of the checkpoint, and the card does not disclose model internals or detailed evaluation data.

possible_risks.description: Proper documentation contains information about how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, including any synthetic data generation processes. Without proper documentation it might be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model.
possible_risks.justification: The card only says RecurrentGemma was trained on the same data and processing as Gemma, without documenting collection, curation, or composition for this checkpoint.

possible_risks.description: Since foundation models can be used for many purposes, a model's intended use is important for defining the relevant risks of that model. As the use changes, the relevant risks might correspondingly change.
possible_risks.justification: The card identifies the model as instruction-tuned text-to-text but does not define intended or prohibited uses, leaving downstream risk scope unspecified.
